question: Do China's item-based export controls on critical minerals (MOFCOM announcements, 2023-07 → 2025-10) move Chinese strategic-materials producers up and the main non-China US rare-earth producer up?

event_filter.source: MOFCOM/MOST item-based export-control announcements on critical minerals and rare-earth technology
scope_rules: Include: new or expanded item-based export controls (global scope, or US-targeted item bans).

Exclude: entity-list actions naming specific foreign firms (Unreliable Entity List, export-control control list), Japan-targeted measures (Jan 2026), suspensions/easing (2025-11-07), enforcement/reporting mechanisms (Announcement 2026 No.26).
Event list assembled from official MOFCOM/MOST pages on 2026-09-22; web timestamps used as event instants.

event_day_rule.US: first NYSE session whose close (16:00 America/New_York) is after eventInstant
event_day_rule.CN: first SSE/SZSE session whose close (15:00 Asia/Shanghai) is after eventInstant

CN_STRATEGIC_MATERIALS.names: 北方稀土, 中国稀土, 盛和资源, 云南锗业, 厦门钨业, 章源钨业
CN_STRATEGIC_MATERIALS.caveat: Chosen in 2026 (survivors); point-in-time eligibility (>=120 pre-event sessions) applies.

US_RARE_EARTH.caveat: Single name; China named MP Materials on its export-control list in June 2026 — an entity action outside this event set.

US_STRATEGIC_METALS_ETF.names: VanEck Rare Earth & Strategic Metals ETF
US_STRATEGIC_METALS_ETF.caveat: Holds Chinese producers as well as non-China names; direction ambiguous, hence secondary.

hypotheses.rationale: Export licensing restricts supply outside China, raising scarcity rents and pricing power for domestic producers.
Non-China supply becomes more valuable; substitution demand and policy support for US producers.
Broad strategic-metals exposure; weaker, mixed prior.

robustness_exclude_reason: Each coincides, within its [0,1] window, with a separate major US–China escalation: C05 follows the US Dec-2024 chip rule by one day; C06 is the Feb-2025 tariff-retaliation package; C07 falls in the Apr-2025 tariff crash; C08's US day+1 is the Oct-10-2025 100% tariff threat.

inference.test: one-sided cross-sectional t on mean CAR across events, plus sign test
inference.placebo: same pipeline on 1,000 random non-event dates

power_note: n = 8 events. With event-level CAR s.d. of a few percent, only large average effects (roughly 3%+) are detectable; a null is weak evidence of no effect.
